title: has_em_dash escape scan is spelling-exact: padded Gleam escapes \u{02014}/\u{002014} compile to U+2014 but evade the lint
evidence:
EM_DASH_ESCAPE = "\\u{2014}"

        idx = literal.find(EM_DASH_ESCAPE, idx)
        if idx < 0:
            return False
        backslashes = 0
        j = idx - 1
        while j >= 0 and literal[j] == "\\":
            backslashes += 1
            j -= 1
        if backslashes % 2 == 0:
            return True  # real escape → an em-dash at runtime

(padded-escape precedent already in the codebase:)
client/src/pages/application_detail_ai.gleam:104:                [html.text("\u{00B7} " <> label)],
detail: Gleam 1.15.1 accepts 1-6 hex digits in \u{...}; verified compile: "\u{02014}" and "\u{002014}" both print U+2014 (E2 80 94). literal.find only matches the exact 7-char spelling, so both padded forms return False. View-module literals (the lint's core target) have no runtime dash scan backstop.
recommended_fix: In has_em_dash, regex-scan the literal for \\u\{([0-9a-fA-F]{1,6})\} and flag when int(codepoint, 16) == 0x2014 and the preceding backslash run is even. Add both padded spellings as probe cases.
